## Unparented

### Repoint pinned referrers in the same write that revises their target

`proposed` · `@akr.work.revise-repoints-pinned-referrers/1`

Revising a record that another live record pins by revision introduces AKR-L021
on the referrer, and the write is refused because that diagnostic is new
(D-039). The referrer cannot be moved to n+1 first because n+1 does not exist
yet. The escape is still a three-write dance: float or drop the pin, revise the
target, re-pin. A single write that rewrites non-historical pins of the retired
revision onto the successor would close
@lege-ecosystem.papercut.healing-an-inherited-akr-t023-on-an-evidence.

**Acceptance** — 0 of 2 satisfied

| Check | Method | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `historical-pins-stay` | command | not satisfied — no evidence |
| `same-write-repoint` | command | not satisfied — no evidence |

### Give the agent scratch directory a lifecycle

`proposed` · `@akr.work.scratch-lifecycle/1`

Give `.agent/scratch/` a lifecycle, so the one disposable directory nothing empties
on its own stops growing until a person clears it by hand.

Measurement and reporting, not deletion by default: `akr check` prints what is there
as a build fact, `knowledge.start` says the same at orientation, and
`akr check --scratch-clean` is the opt-in gate. `akr scratch prune` removes unkept
entries by age and `akr scratch keep` protects one with a reason, so an agent can
tidy up at the end of a session without being able to delete what the next session
was told to expect. See D-036.
